A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAMeLU research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support comparison despite substantial experimental revisions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original few-shot classification experiments, learning curves, feature-extractor ablations, and task-generation analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification results and ablations, including additional Meta-iNat evaluations, BECLR comparisons, clustering-based task generation, and a one-query experiment.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the specified query construction from mixing an existing support image with another image to mixing a separately augmented view of the support source image. ResNet-50 replaces CLIP as the default extractor, although both architectures were already evaluated in v1. The class encoder, transformer-based inference, and training objective remain.

E1.justification: Meta-iNat adds another fine-grained classification domain for evaluation and baseline training, extending coverage beyond the four retained benchmarks. The few-shot task family remains unchanged. ImageNet-964, miniImageNet, MSCOCO, and Fungi training experiments remain present; multi-dataset training moves to Appendix A.3.

E2.justification: The small-scale training comparison adds BECLR alongside PsCo and CAMeLU (v1 Table 8 versus v2 Tables 2 and 11). Appendix A.5 also introduces a k-means task-generation comparator. The existing external baseline families remain represented.

E3.justification: The main CAMeLU configuration changes from CLIP-ViT-B/16 to supervised ResNet-50 pretrained on ImageNet-964, increasing the transformer input width from 1024 to 2304. Cross-domain PsCo training changes from ImageNet-1k to ImageNet-964 to remove overlap with miniImageNet evaluation classes. Appendix A.1 changes image normalization from [0,1] to zero mean and unit variance. Appendix A.7 adds a one-query evaluation condition; these are substantive reported setting changes.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands task-generation testing with quantitative augmentation-only and k-means comparisons in Table 7, replacing v1's leakage-versus-no-leakage learning-curve comparison. It adds an extractor-pretraining overlap control and a one-query analysis. The embedding case study gains centroid distances while dropping the CIFAR-fs illustration. Pixel-versus-patch mixing, Beta-parameter sensitivity, and logistic learning-phase analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across three complete runs, with evaluation averaged over 500 tasks. v2 relocates the main tables' standard deviations to Appendix A.10 rather than removing uncertainty reporting. No new statistical testing or repeated-run practice is specified.

E6.justification: Main and ablation results are extensively replaced or supplemented. For example, Table 1's CAMeLU miniImageNet 1-shot/5-shot accuracies change from 69.63/90.95 to 76.51/92.14 under revised settings, so these are not same-setting gains. New Meta-iNat, BECLR, clustering, and one-query results appear. The small-scale CAML learning curve changes from increasing in v1 Figure 6 to approximately flat in v2 Figure 3.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 restores the missing '1 minus' in the simplified class-collision probability, correcting its inconsistency with the preceding expression. Appendix A.7 adds a computational-cost argument of O(Q(NK+1)^2 d). The existing training formulation and logistic-phase mathematics remain, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about unsupervised task creation, in-context learning, and prediction without fine-tuning remain. The introduction changes superiority across 'all datasets' to 'several datasets,' and the introduction and conclusion relax the main hardware-efficiency claim from 4GB to 8GB VRAM.

C2.justification: Multi-dataset training is reinterpreted as offering little benefit to CAMeLU because task generation already supplies diversity, replacing v1's modest-improvement interpretation. The default extractor is now justified by comparison fairness, and Appendix A.7 qualifies scalability through quadratic support-set cost. Existing noisy-data and fixed-way limitations remain after relocation.

D1.justification: Implementation documentation updates the GPU from an RTX 3050 Ti with 4GB to an RTX 3070 Ti with 8GB, describes ResNet-50 pretraining and BECLR configuration, and identifies 25 queries for the main comparison. Code release remains promised upon acceptance. Appendix A.1 introduces an inconsistent CLIP description that reverses the earlier image-feature and concatenated-input dimensions.

R1.justification: v2 adds BECLR and distinguishes its contrastive few-shot framework from meta-learning. It also adds citations for deep residual learning and the Meta-iNat source. The broader positioning relative to UML, image mixing, and in-context learning remains intact.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: small-scale generalization moves from Appendix 7.6 to Section 4.5, multi-dataset training moves from Section 4.5 to Appendix A.3, and limitations move to Appendix A.9. Appendix analyses are reordered, with embedding analysis brought forward, and several experimental explanations are rewritten.

P2.justification: Main comparison tables are redesigned with Meta-iNat columns and means only, while full uncertainty tables are redisplayed in Appendix A.10. A new task-generation ablation table is added. The embedding figure is substantially redrawn with shaded clusters, centroids, and distances; learning-curve displays are revised and several figures and tables are relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the main comparison by replacing v1's mismatched default backbones and leakage-affected PsCo evaluation with common ResNet-50/ImageNet-964 settings. Additional task-generation controls and the BECLR comparison better test the method's contribution beyond its feature extractor. New reporting defects, including reversed CLIP dimensions in A.1 and inconsistent multi-dataset values between Tables 5 and 6(b), limit reproducibility, but the improved experimental controls provide a substantial net gain in evidential quality.
